# SplitMix64

The seeding generator: a fast mixer with a 64-bit state, used to spread one seed over a larger one.

```rux
pub struct SplitMix64 {
    // private fields
}
```

Not for general use — its period is only 2^64 and it fails statistical tests a real generator passes. Its
job is the one thing it is very good at: turning a seed a human chose, which is very likely to be zero or
one or a timestamp, into a full-entropy state for a generator that deserves better input than that. Seeding
a 256-bit generator by copying a small integer into one word and leaving the rest zero is a classic way to
get correlated streams out of an excellent algorithm.

```rux
pub func SplitMix64(seed: uint64) -> SplitMix64
```

A mixer starting from `seed`. Every seed is acceptable, including zero.

## Implements RandomGenerator

<h3 id="next-uint64"><code>NextUint64</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NextUint64(self: &var SplitMix64) -> uint64
```

The next word: the state advanced by an odd constant, then avalanched.
The additive step guarantees the full period of 2^64 whatever the seed, and the mixing afterwards is
what turns a counter into something that looks random. Both constants are Steele, Lea and Flood's.

**Returns**: the next 64 bits

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Generator.rux#L54)
